column2: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India
column12: Whether the twin conditions for bail in s 45 PMLA are constitutionally valid.
column13: Twin conditions upheld as a reasonable regime for a special law on money laundering; they apply whatever form the bail relief takes.
column14: Nikesh Tarachand Shah v. Union of India (2018) 11 SCC 1 [VERIFY]

column2: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation (Sisodia I)
column12: Whether bail should be granted to a former Delhi Deputy Chief Minister in the excise-policy case.
column13: Bail refused at that stage, with liberty to apply again after about three months if the trial was slow.

column2: Tarsem Lal v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether an accused who appears on a summons after the Special Court takes cognizance must satisfy the twin conditions.
column13: No; such an accused is not in custody, so the ED cannot arrest him without the court's permission and ordinary bail law applies.

column2: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement (Sisodia II)
column12: Whether about 17 months in custody with no prospect of an early trial justifies bail despite s 45.
column13: Bail granted; the right to speedy trial under Art 21 prevails when trial cannot realistically start soon.
column14: Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb (2021) [VERIFY]

column2: K. Kavitha v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether bail was wrongly refused to a woman accused under the first proviso to s 45(1).
column13: Bail granted; the proviso for women and the Sisodia reasoning on custody and delay were applied.
column14: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement (2024) [VERIFY]

column2: Prem Prakash v. Union of India
column12: Whether long custody and a slow trial justify bail without satisfying the twin conditions.
column13: Bail granted; s 45 was read together with Art 21 and the principle that bail is the rule. [VERIFY]
column14: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement (2024)

column2: V. Senthil Balaji v. Deputy Director, Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether a former minister held for about 15 months should get bail when the trial is unlikely to end soon.
column13: Bail granted; where the maximum sentence is seven years, prolonged pre-trial custody can outweigh the statutory restriction.
column14: Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb (2021) [VERIFY]

column2: Padam Chand Jain v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether bail can follow the Sisodia reasoning when co-accused are already out and evidence is mostly documentary.
column13: Bail granted; twin conditions cannot override Art 21, and Sisodia's bail was not an Art 142 order.
column14: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement (2024)

column2: Directorate of Enforcement v. Subhash Sharma
column12: Whether bail can be refused for failing the twin conditions when the arrest itself was illegal.
column13: No; if the arrest violated Arts 21 and 22, the court must grant bail whether or not the twin conditions are met.

column2: Union of India v. Kanhaiya Prasad
column12: Whether a High Court can grant bail without recording satisfaction on the twin conditions.
column13: No; the twin conditions are mandatory, so the bail order was set aside, remanded to another bench and the accused told to surrender.
column14: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India (2022)

column2: Udhaw Singh v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether over a year in custody with a distant trial justifies bail despite s 45.
column13: Bail granted; constitutional courts may grant bail under PMLA when the trial will be unduly delayed; Kanhaiya Prasad distinguished.
column14: V. Senthil Balaji v. Deputy Director, ED (2024)

column2: Arvind Dham v. Directorate of Enforcement
column12: Whether about 16 months in custody with no cognizance taken justifies bail in a large bank-fraud money-laundering case.
column13: Bail granted; speedy trial under Art 21 is not eclipsed by the nature of the offence, and economic offences are not one class.
column14: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement (2024)

column2: Directorate of Enforcement v. Aditya Tripathi
column12: Whether a High Court could grant bail without applying s 45 merely because the investigation was done and a charge sheet filed.
column13: High Court bail orders set aside and the bail pleas sent back for fresh decision under s 45.
